layers.title: Lake Victoria Basin boundary
layers.source: ICPAC geoportal (geonode:lv_basin), 2019; lake shoreline from the Copernicus GLO-30 water-body mask (2011-2015), class 2 at native ~30 m, islands as holes
layers.licence: ICPAC: not specified (confirm before public release); WBM: Copernicus, free with attribution
layers.caveats: Lake shoreline from the Copernicus GLO-30 water-body mask (2011-2015); it predates the 2020/2024 high stands.

layers.title: Flood hazard (observed flood frequency)

query.wording: flooded in up to {N} of 10 years within 100 m

layers.source: Copernicus EMS Global Flood Monitoring (Sentinel-1), 20 m, 2016-2025
layers.units: band1: years flooded (0-10); band2: % of valid obs; band3: % excluded
layers.citation: Salamon et al. (2021) IGARSS, doi:10.1109/IGARSS47720.2021.9554214. Contains modified Copernicus EMS information (2016-2025). Hazard proxy, not risk.
layers.caveats: Flooded vegetation and urban areas under-detected; short floods between overpasses missed; band 3 shows where SAR cannot map floods.

layers.title: Terrain (Copernicus GLO-30)
layers.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (~30 m), basin extent
layers.licence: Copernicus DEM: free use with attribution
layers.citation: ESA (2021). Copernicus DEM GLO-30. Contains modified Copernicus data.
layers.caveats: The DEM export is a union of two rectangles; areas outside it (all outside the basin: north-west of 31E/1N, the far south-east and south-west corners) and the 600 km display padding hold synthetic filler. Elevations are neither shown nor queryable anywhere; the basin itself has full real GLO-30 coverage.

layers.title: Precipitation (CHIRPS v3)

palette.value: cividis reversed (dry yellow -> wet dark blue)

layers.source: CHIRPS v3.0 daily, 0.05 deg. CHIRPS is a pentad product; daily values are pentad totals disaggregated with ECMWF ERA5 precipitation (the 'rnl' flavour).
layers.caveats: Satellite rainfall over the lake surface is less reliable; basin means use land cells only.
layers.citation: Funk et al. (2015), Scientific Data 2:150066; CHIRPS v3.0, UCSB Climate Hazards Center

layers.title: Temperature (CHIRTS-ERA5)
layers.citation: Funk et al. (2019), J. Climate 32:5639-5658; CHIRTS-ERA5, UCSB CHC

layers.title: Satellite imagery (Sentinel-2)
layers.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data: free use with attribution

layers.title: Lake water level (satellite altimetry)
layers.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (DAHITI terms of use; non-commercial use only)
layers.citation: Schwatke, C., Dettmering, D., Bosch, W., Seitz, F. (2015), HESS 19, 4345–4364, doi:10.5194/hess-19-4345-2015

layers.title: Drought index (SPI-3)

palette.value: BrBG diverging, centred 0, fixed -3..3 (values clipped to ±3)

layers.source: SPI-3 computed from CHIRPS v3.0 monthly totals (gamma fit, Thom 1958; zero-rain mixed distribution), calibration 1991-2020. Daily CHIRPS = ERA5-disaggregated pentads ('rnl'); monthly totals are unaffected by the disaggregation choice.
layers.citation: McKee, Doesken & Kleist (1993), 8th Conf. Applied Climatology; classes: WMO (2012), SPI User Guide, WMO-No. 1090; Funk et al. (2015), Scientific Data 2:150066

layers.title: Rivers (HydroRIVERS)
layers.source: HydroRIVERS v1.0 (HydroSHEDS), Strahler order >= 4, clipped to the basin
layers.licence: HydroSHEDS v1 licence (WWF; HydroSHEDS Technical Documentation v1.4, Appendix A). Incorporates data from the HydroSHEDS version 1 database, © World Wildlife Fund, Inc. (2006-2022), used under license; full attribution in the data README
layers.citation: Lehner, B. & Grill, G. (2013). Hydrological Processes 27(15):2171-2186; Lehner, B., Verdin, K., Jarvis, A. (2008): New global hydrography derived from spaceborne elevation data. Eos, Transactions, AGU, 89(10): 93-94. www.hydrosheds.org
layers.caveats: The Yala main stem (Strahler >= 4) ends at the Yala Swamp, about 6 km from open water; only lower-order swamp channels reach the lake (HydroRIVERS v1.0).

layers.title: Population (exposure input)
layers.source: WorldPop constrained individual countries 2020, 100 m (KEN, UGA, TZA, RWA, BDI)
layers.release_note: 2020 constrained (Global 2000-2020, BSGM/maxar): no newer constrained release was found on hub.worldpop.org at build time
layers.caveats: Exposure input (people in place), not risk; census-era modelled counts.
layers.citation: WorldPop (2020), School of Geography and Environmental Science, University of Southampton. doi:10.5258/SOTON/WP00682

layers.title: Tree-cover loss (Hansen GFC)
layers.source: Hansen Global Forest Change GFC-2025-v1.13; loss where tree cover 2000 >= 30 %
layers.caveats: Tree-cover loss, not deforestation; only where cover 2000 >= 30 %; detection improved ~2011-2013, annual values not strictly comparable across the break. Map shows cumulative loss at 5-year epochs (MapLibre cannot style rasters by value); the panel reports exact annual areas.
layers.citation: Hansen et al. (2013), Science 342:850-853. Data: UMD/Google/USGS/NASA.

layers.title: Active fires (VIIRS)
layers.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active fires; density: S-NPP only (2012-2025); points: S-NPP + NOAA-20 (NOAA-20 archive from 2020); confidence nominal/high
layers.caveats: Mostly savanna and crop-residue burning; charcoal production not detected reliably; cloud hides wet-season fires. NOAA-20 only in the point layer.
layers.citation: NASA FIRMS; Schroeder et al. (2014), RSE 143:85-96. doi:10.5067/FIRMS/VIIRS/VNP14IMGT

layers.title: Burned area (MODIS)
layers.source: MODIS MCD64A1 v6.1 monthly burned area, annual union per ~500 m cell, via Microsoft Planetary Computer
layers.units: burned at least once in the year (0/1)
layers.caveats: ~500 m detection misses small/low-intensity burns; cloud limits wet-season detection.
layers.range_note: annual burned area in the basin, all years 2001-2025: min 4100 km2 (2017), median 10296 km2, max 15323 km2 (2003)

layers.title: Land cover (Esri/IO annual)
layers.source: Esri/Impact Observatory annual LULC v2 (10 m; displayed at 30 m, nearest), via Microsoft Planetary Computer (io-lulc-annual-v02)
layers.period: 2017-2023 (no 2024 release on Planetary Computer at build time, probed 2026-10-21)
layers.caveats: Global land-cover products disagree on cropland in sub-Saharan Africa (Kerner et al. 2023); year-to-year change is indicative.
layers.citation: Karra et al. (2021), IGARSS; Impact Observatory, Esri, Microsoft.

layers.title: Land cover reference (ESA WorldCover 2021)
layers.source: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200 (displayed at 30 m, nearest)
layers.citation: Zanaga et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7254221

layers.title: Place names
layers.source: OpenStreetMap via the Protomaps daily basemap (build 2026-10-22, schema v4, Planetiler 0.10.2)
layers.units: labels only: countries, cities, towns, villages (from z11), lakes, rivers, protected areas
layers.citation: © OpenStreetMap contributors (openstreetmap.org/copyright). Basemap tiles: Protomaps (protomaps.com). Fonts: Noto Sans (SIL Open Font License) via protomaps/basemaps-assets.
layers.caveats: Volunteered geographic information: coverage and spelling vary; label positions are OSM points, not authoritative gazetteer locations.

layers.title: Admin boundaries
layers.source: geoBoundaries gbOpen ADM1 + ADM2 (simplified), Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi; clipped to the basin
layers.period: boundary years vary by country (2006-2021; see provenance)
layers.units: ADM1 and ADM2 polygons; names at mid zoom
layers.licence: per boundary - see provenance (Public Domain, CC0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY 3.0 IGO, ODbL); geoBoundaries itself CC BY 4.0
layers.citation: Runfola, D. et al. (2020) geoBoundaries: A global database of political administrative boundaries. PLoS ONE 15(4): e0231866. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0231866
layers.caveats: Boundaries are indicative and not an official delimitation. Uganda ADM1 is the 4 regions (2017, from OSM) and ADM2 the 2006 counties; Tanzania ADM1 is OSM-derived. Not GADM.
